statement: For every input satisfying the preconditions, minimum_semesters(n, relations) returns a result r; it does not fail.
preconditions: 1 <= n <= 5000; 0 <= len(relations) <= 5000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(relations), len(relations[i]) = 2; letting a = relations[i][0] and b = relations[i][1], we have 1 <= a <= n, 1 <= b <= n, and a != b; and for every i,j with 0 <= i < len(relations), 0 <= j < len(relations), and i != j, relations[i] != relations[j].

statement: Whenever minimum_semesters(n, relations) returns a result r, either r = -1 or 1 <= r <= n.
preconditions: 1 <= n <= 5000; 0 <= len(relations) <= 5000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(relations), len(relations[i]) = 2; letting a = relations[i][0] and b = relations[i][1], we have 1 <= a <= n, 1 <= b <= n, and a != b; and for every i,j with 0 <= i < len(relations), 0 <= j < len(relations), and i != j, relations[i] != relations[j].

statement: The function returns a result r, and r is characterized as follows. For an integer k >= 1, call a total function sem from {1,...,n} to {1,...,k} a k-semester schedule if for every relation [a,b] appearing in relations we have sem(a) < sem(b). If there exists a k-semester schedule for some k >= 1, then r is the least such k; otherwise r = -1.
preconditions: 1 <= n <= 5000; 0 <= len(relations) <= 5000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(relations), len(relations[i]) = 2; letting a = relations[i][0] and b = relations[i][1], we have 1 <= a <= n, 1 <= b <= n, and a != b; and for every i,j with 0 <= i < len(relations), 0 <= j < len(relations), and i != j, relations[i] != relations[j].

statement: Whenever minimum_semesters(n, relations) returns a result r, r = 1 if and only if len(relations) = 0.
preconditions: 1 <= n <= 5000; 0 <= len(relations) <= 5000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(relations), len(relations[i]) = 2; letting a = relations[i][0] and b = relations[i][1], we have 1 <= a <= n, 1 <= b <= n, and a != b; and for every i,j with 0 <= i < len(relations), 0 <= j < len(relations), and i != j, relations[i] != relations[j].

statement: Whenever minimum_semesters(n, relations) returns a result r, r = -1 if and only if the directed graph on vertices {1,...,n} with an edge a -> b for each relation [a,b] in relations contains a directed cycle, that is, there exist L >= 1 and courses c_0,...,c_L such that c_L = c_0, each c_i is in {1,...,n}, and for every j with 0 <= j < L the ordered pair [c_j,c_{j+1}] is in relations.
preconditions: 1 <= n <= 5000; 0 <= len(relations) <= 5000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(relations), len(relations[i]) = 2; letting a = relations[i][0] and b = relations[i][1], we have 1 <= a <= n, 1 <= b <= n, and a != b; and for every i,j with 0 <= i < len(relations), 0 <= j < len(relations), and i != j, relations[i] != relations[j].

statement: Under these additional preconditions, minimum_semesters(n, relations) returns n.
preconditions: 1 <= n <= 5000; 0 <= len(relations) <= 5000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(relations), len(relations[i]) = 2; letting a = relations[i][0] and b = relations[i][1], we have 1 <= a <= n, 1 <= b <= n, and a != b; and for every i,j with 0 <= i < len(relations), 0 <= j < len(relations), and i != j, relations[i] != relations[j]. Additionally, there exists a sequence c_1,...,c_n of courses such that {c_1,...,c_n} = {1,...,n} and relations consists exactly of the n-1 ordered pairs [c_i,c_{i+1}] for 1 <= i < n.

statement: Whenever minimum_semesters(n, relations) returns a result r with r != -1, there exists a total function sem from {1,...,n} to {1,...,r} such that for every relation [a,b] in relations we have sem(a) < sem(b).
preconditions: 1 <= n <= 5000; 0 <= len(relations) <= 5000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(relations), len(relations[i]) = 2; letting a = relations[i][0] and b = relations[i][1], we have 1 <= a <= n, 1 <= b <= n, and a != b; and for every i,j with 0 <= i < len(relations), 0 <= j < len(relations), and i != j, relations[i] != relations[j].

statement: Whenever minimum_semesters(n, relations) returns a result r with r != -1, for every integer k with 1 <= k < r there does not exist a total function sem from {1,...,n} to {1,...,k} such that for every relation [a,b] in relations we have sem(a) < sem(b).
preconditions: 1 <= n <= 5000; 0 <= len(relations) <= 5000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(relations), len(relations[i]) = 2; letting a = relations[i][0] and b = relations[i][1], we have 1 <= a <= n, 1 <= b <= n, and a != b; and for every i,j with 0 <= i < len(relations), 0 <= j < len(relations), and i != j, relations[i] != relations[j].

statement: Whenever minimum_semesters(n, relations) returns a result r with r != -1, for every L >= 0 and every sequence of courses c_0,...,c_L such that for each j with 0 <= j < L the ordered pair [c_j,c_{j+1}] is in relations, we have r >= L+1.
preconditions: 1 <= n <= 5000; 0 <= len(relations) <= 5000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(relations), len(relations[i]) = 2; letting a = relations[i][0] and b = relations[i][1], we have 1 <= a <= n, 1 <= b <= n, and a != b; and for every i,j with 0 <= i < len(relations), 0 <= j < len(relations), and i != j, relations[i] != relations[j].

statement: Whenever minimum_semesters(n, relations) returns a result r with r != -1, there exists a sequence of courses c_0,...,c_{r-1} such that each c_i is in {1,...,n} and for every j with 0 <= j < r-1 the ordered pair [c_j,c_{j+1}] is in relations.
preconditions: 1 <= n <= 5000; 0 <= len(relations) <= 5000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(relations), len(relations[i]) = 2; letting a = relations[i][0] and b = relations[i][1], we have 1 <= a <= n, 1 <= b <= n, and a != b; and for every i,j with 0 <= i < len(relations), 0 <= j < len(relations), and i != j, relations[i] != relations[j].

statement: Whenever minimum_semesters(n, relations) returns a result r and minimum_semesters(n, relations2) returns a result r2, we have r = r2.
preconditions: 1 <= n <= 5000. relations and relations2 each satisfy: 0 <= len(relations) <= 5000 and 0 <= len(relations2) <= 5000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(relations), len(relations[i]) = 2; letting a = relations[i][0] and b = relations[i][1], 1 <= a <= n, 1 <= b <= n, and a != b; all ordered pairs in relations are distinct; and the analogous conditions hold with relations2 in place of relations. Also relations2 is a permutation of relations: len(relations2) = len(relations) and there exists a bijection f from {0,...,len(relations)-1} to {0,...,len(relations2)-1} such that relations[i] = relations2[f(i)] for every i.

statement: Let r1 be the result of minimum_semesters(n, relations1) and r2 be the result of minimum_semesters(n, relations2). Whenever both calls return results, if r2 != -1 then r1 != -1 and r1 <= r2.
preconditions: 1 <= n <= 5000. relations1 and relations2 each satisfy: 0 <= len(relations1) <= 5000 and 0 <= len(relations2) <= 5000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(relations1), len(relations1[i]) = 2; letting a = relations1[i][0] and b = relations1[i][1], 1 <= a <= n, 1 <= b <= n, and a != b; all ordered pairs in relations1 are distinct; and the analogous conditions hold for relations2. Also, for every i with 0 <= i < len(relations1), the ordered pair relations1[i] occurs in relations2, i.e. there exists j with 0 <= j < len(relations2) such that relations2[j] = relations1[i].

statement: Whenever minimum_semesters(n, relations) returns a result r with r != -1, there exists a total function sem from {1,...,n} to {1,...,r} such that for every relation [a,b] in relations we have sem(a) < sem(b), and for every s with 1 <= s <= r there exists a course c in {1,...,n} with sem(c) = s.
preconditions: 1 <= n <= 5000; 0 <= len(relations) <= 5000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(relations), len(relations[i]) = 2; letting a = relations[i][0] and b = relations[i][1], we have 1 <= a <= n, 1 <= b <= n, and a != b; and for every i,j with 0 <= i < len(relations), 0 <= j < len(relations), and i != j, relations[i] != relations[j].

statement: Whenever minimum_semesters(n, relations) returns r and minimum_semesters(n, relations2) returns r2, we have r = r2; that is, renaming the course labels does not change the minimum number of semesters, including the -1 case.
preconditions: 1 <= n <= 5000; relations and relations2 are arrays of ordered pairs of courses satisfying the base input conditions: 0 <= len <= 5000, every entry has length 2, both entries lie in {1,...,n}, no pair has equal endpoints, and within each array all ordered pairs are distinct. Additionally, there exists a permutation pi of {1,...,n} such that relations2 consists exactly of the ordered pairs [pi(a), pi(b)] for every [a,b] in relations.
